items.title: A framework for verifiable analysis of AI behavior
items.raw_excerpt: Developing an AI agent is a complex data analysis problem. To know if the agent is working correctly, we need to track not just benchmark scores but the details of its behavior: how do the strategies change over the course of training? Why does the new scaffold perform worse? Is there reward hacking? Answering these questions requires a combination of quantitative and qualitative analysis tailored to the dataset at hand.

excerpt_i18n.en: While the entire industry is racing to build large models and agents—the brains of the AI era—Huawei has set its sights on the nerve endings of the entire system. During HDC 2026, Huawei decided to fully open-source the SparkLink protocol stack to the OpenHarmony community in July 2026. This short-range communication capability, previously confined to Huawei's terminal products, will be made available to the entire industry chain in open-source form for the first time. For a long time, Wi-Fi and Bluetooth have driven the wireless revolution, freeing devices from cables and bringing headphones, mice, watches, speakers, and various smart home devices into daily life. However, as AIoT enters a deeper stage of development, device connections have shifted from single-point networking to multi-device collaboration, and user demands for connectivity have evolved. In the past, simply pairing and connecting was sufficient; now, connections must be stable, responsive, and capable of supporting more devices simultaneously. These connectivity challenges are precisely the gaps that SparkLink has already addressed, indicating that SparkLink still has a long way to go. "Open-sourcing" SparkLink marks a transition from technological breakthroughs to industry-wide adoption. In the past development of Huawei's SparkLink, many partners have already participated, with Huawei being one of them. According to Qin Yao, Vice President of Industry Development at Huawei's Terminal BG, as introduced to Leiphone, SparkLink adopts a layered design, similar to the logic of mobile communications and Bluetooth technology, consisting of a bottom access layer, a middle service layer, and an upper application layer. Among these, the access layer is deeply tied to hardware, led by HiSilicon, with contributions from Telink and Maxscend.
excerpt_i18n.es: Mientras toda la industria compite por desarrollar grandes modelos y agentes, los "cerebros" de la era de la IA, Huawei ha dirigido su atención a las terminaciones nerviosas de todo el sistema. Durante el HDC 2026, Huawei decidió liberar completamente el protocolo StarFlash en la comunidad OpenHarmony en julio de 2026. Esta capacidad de comunicación de corto alcance, que antes solo pertenecía a los productos terminales de Huawei, se abrirá por primera vez a toda la cadena industrial en forma de código abierto. Durante mucho tiempo, Wi-Fi y Bluetooth han popularizado la conectividad inalámbrica. Han liberado a los dispositivos de los cables y han integrado auriculares, ratones, relojes, altavoces y diversos dispositivos inteligentes para el hogar en la vida cotidiana.

At the China Auto Chongqing Forum, invited by Leiphone, during a seminar themed "OEMs X Tech Companies: How to Define the Next-Generation Car," Liu Yuxiang, Director of Product Planning and Definition at Changan Automobile, used this statement to summarize the changes occurring in the definition of automobiles in the AI era. In recent years, the automotive industry's discussion of intelligence has largely revolved around specific functions, with different systems upgrading independently, forming the main content of the previous stage of smart car competition. However, in the AI-driven phase, such single-point upgrades are no longer sufficient to explain the changes in next-generation cars. Liu Yuxiang believes that future cars will increasingly resemble a system centrally coordinated by a central brain, where the chassis, powertrain, cockpit, intelligent driving, and cloud no longer operate independently but need to be reorganized by the vehicle's overall intelligence. At this seminar, guests from OEMs, intelligent cockpit providers, automotive electronics companies, global parts suppliers, consumer electronics manufacturers, and autonomous driving logistics companies also offered similar judgments from their respective industry positions. Although their starting points differed, a consensus emerged: after AI enters the automotive sector, the changes go beyond adding a large model to the cockpit or enabling voice assistants to answer more questions. Instead, cars will transform from mechanical-electronic products into mobile intelligent entities capable of perception, decision-making, coordination, and continuous evolution. The core of the next-generation car is not single-point intelligence but vehicle-wide intelligence. In the past, automotive intelligence was largely advanced by domain. Intelligent driving had its own system.

excerpt_i18n.en:
Recently, the "Computing-Power Grid: AI+Energy Bidirectional Empowerment" seminar, hosted by the China Academy of Information and Communications Technology, was successfully held in Beijing. During the event, the SenseSynergy computing-power grid collaboration Agent platform passed the "Computing-Power Grid Collaboration Platform Capability Testing Method," becoming the first Agent platform in the industry to pass this test. The evaluation covered 16 test items across four capability areas: intelligent query and Q&A, load and power consumption prediction, electricity pricing and cost analysis, and energy storage strategy management. The SenseSynergy computing-power grid collaboration Agent platform excelled in all indicators, fully demonstrating its industry-leading capabilities in real-time computing-power and electricity coordination, AIDC cost reduction and efficiency improvement, and AI-driven intelligent decision-making and scheduling.  

01. Data-Driven + AI Empowerment: Industry-Leading Computing-Power Grid Collaboration Agent Platform  

SenseTime's large-scale AI infrastructure believes that AIDC in the AI era represents an upgraded evolution from traditional IDC to intelligent infrastructure, essentially functioning as a "smart factory" that continuously produces tokens. The key to future competition in the AI industry will no longer be solely about how much computing power one possesses, but rather who can more efficiently convert electricity, computing power, and data into valuable tokens.  

Based on this insight, SenseTime's large-scale AI infrastructure has developed the SenseSynergy computing-power grid collaboration Agent, introducing the Agent concept into the operational scenarios of intelligent computing centers. This creates an AI scheduling system that can perceive, think, make decisions, execute actions, and continuously evolve.
excerpt_i18n.es: Recientemente, el seminario "Tejido de cómputo y electricidad: empoderamiento bidireccional de IA+Energía", organizado por la Academia de Tecnología de la Información y las Comunicaciones de China, se celebró con éxito en Pekín. Durante el evento, la plataforma SenseSynergy, un agente de colaboración entre cómputo y electricidad, superó la prueba del "Método de evaluación de capacidades de plataformas de colaboración entre cómputo y electricidad", convirtiéndose en la primera plataforma de este tipo en la industria en pasar dicha evaluación. La prueba abarcó 16 ítems en cuatro áreas principales: consulta y respuesta inteligente, predicción de carga y consumo, análisis de precios de electricidad y gestión de estrategias de almacenamiento de energía. SenseSynergy obtuvo un rendimiento sobresaliente en todos los indicadores, lo que demuestra plenamente su capacidad para la colaboración en tiempo real entre cómputo y electricidad, así como para la reducción de costos en centros de datos de inteligencia artificial (AIDC).
